feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration 6 design (best raced score 184.93: kp 3.0, ki 0.8, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016, last_direction) with one change, ki from 0.8 to 1.0. All values are inside the contract limits, and the change is a clean single-variable step on the lever that has helped at each prior step. Iteration 6 raised ki from 0.4 to 0.8 and the score rose from 175.70 to 184.93, with s-bend progress up from 0.40 to 0.45. Max_error stays near 0.06 to 0.064 m on every track, which is consistent with a residual steady offset. Earlier evidence still rejects wider outer sensors (iteration 3, 54.87), higher kp (iteration 4, 108.24), and lower base_speed (iteration 2, 115.67), so those stay fixed. The main risk is that steering_oscillation on the s-bend was 0.337 at ki 0.8, close to the 0.35 limit, so extra integral gain could push jitter up. After the race, compare the score against 184.93 and check progress on s-bend and slalom, max_error, steering_oscillation, line_loss_events, and oval completion_time. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on any track, return ki to 0.8 (the iteration 6 fallback). If the score is at or above 184.93 with progress unchanged or higher, keep ki 1.0 and consider one further step only if oscillation stays clear of the limit. If the score falls below 184.93 with progress unchanged, keep iteration 6.
requested_changes: After the race, if steering_oscillation on the s-bend or oval exceeds about 0.35, return ki to 0.8 (the iteration 6 value, score 184.93) and keep kd 0.5, since oscillation was already 0.337 on the s-bend at ki 0.8.

If the score rises above 184.93 with s-bend progress at or above 0.45 and slalom progress at or above 0.12, consider ki 1.2 as the next single step, with all other fields unchanged, to see whether the steady offset keeps shrinking.

Do not change sensor positions, kp, kd, or base_speed in this step. Iterations 2, 3, and 4 showed those moves lowered the score relative to the best design, and iteration 5 showed kd 0.5 is the current best damping.
